{{Quote|First Order went after us—leaders from the old wars. They took our kids. My girl wasn't even old enough to walk. Far as I know, she's a stormtrooper now.|Landonis Balthazar Calrissian|<ref name="TROS Expanded Edition" />}}
'''Kadara Calrissian'''<ref name="Shadow of the Sith" /> was a [[Gender|female]] individual and the daughter of [[Landonis Balthazar Calrissian]]. In the [[Standard year|years]] of peace after the [[Galactic Civil War]], Calrissian attempted to start a [[Calrissian family|family]], and his daughter was [[Reproduction|born]]<ref name="IX TVD" /> in [[13 ABY]].<ref name="Timelines" /> In the time they were together, he was a loving [[Parent|father]],<ref name="Galactic Guide">''[[Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Galactic Guide]]''</ref> however in [[15 ABY]], when she was two years old, she was kidnapped by the [[First Order]],<ref name="Timelines" /> along with other children of former [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel]] leaders.<ref name="TROS Expanded Edition" />

After the tragedy of losing his daughter and his failure in a [[Mission to Pasaana|quest]] with [[Luke Skywalker]] to find answers about the growing [[Dark side of the Force|darkness]] in [[the Force]], Calrissian settled on the [[desert]] [[planet]] of [[Pasaana]] to lead the life of a "[[hermit]]". At first, [[Exile (punishment)|exiling]] himself and hoping to bury his painful memories, he found comfort from the modest and friendly [[Homeworld|native]] [[Aki-Aki]] communities and the simplified life centered him.<ref name="IX TVD" /> After the [[Battle of Exegol]], Lando's hopes for finding his daughter were renewed by an encounter with [[Jannah]], who was a [[Company 77|former stormtrooper]] herself. Having resolved to provide whatever assistance he could offer to the countless individuals that the First Order had stolen from their [[homeworld]]s, Lando, although he acknowledged it as being unlikely, hoped that he might find his daughter in the process.<ref name="TROS Expanded Edition" />

==Behind the scenes==
Landonis Balthazar Calrissian's daughter was first mentioned in the [[2019]] reference books ''[[Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary]]'' by [[Pablo Hidalgo]]<ref name="IX TVD" /> and ''[[Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Galactic Guide]]'' by [[Matt Jones]].<ref name="Galactic Guide" /> Although his daughter was not mentioned in the [[Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker|film]] itself,<ref name="Episode IX">{{Film|IX}}</ref> Calrissian referenced the kidnappings of former Rebel leaders' children by the First Order that she was a victim of in lines from a [[Content cut from Star Wars|deleted scene]] published in ''The Visual Dictionary''.<ref name="IX TVD" /> According to co-writer [[Chris Terrio]], Lando's revelation about his daughter being kidnapped was meant to give greater context to the targeting of [[Ben Solo]].<ref name="Art of TROS">''[[The Art of Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker]]''</ref> She was first identified as "Kadara" in [[Adam Christopher]]'s [[2022]] novel ''[[Shadow of the Sith]]''.<ref name="Shadow of the Sith" /> Kadara's name was a reference to Lando's original name of "Lando Kadar" in [[Leigh Brackett]]'s script for the [[1980]] film [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']].<ref name="Adam Christopher">{{Twitter|ghostfinder|status/1545480601595256833|[[Adam Christopher]]|date=2022-07-08|quote=@ElijahSawyer7 Yep.|archivedate=https://web.archive.org/web/20220708185727/https://twitter.com/ghostfinder/status/1545480601595256833}}</ref>
